title: Why Do Mirrors Flip Left and Right But Not Up and Down?
description:
It's one of the oldest puzzles in physics — and almost everyone gets the answer wrong. A mirror seems to swap your left and right, yet it never flips your head and your feet. So what is it really doing? The truth isn't about left and right at all. It's about front and back, a hidden property called chirality, and the quiet trick your own brain plays every time you look at your reflection. Once you see it, you can't unsee it.

scenes.narration: Here is a question that has puzzled people for over two thousand years.
Why does a mirror flip your left and your right, but never your top and your bottom?
Stay with me, because the real answer is stranger than it sounds.
Stand in front of a mirror and slowly raise your right hand.
The figure staring back raises what looks like its left hand instead.
Now hold a page of writing up to the glass.
Every word snaps into reverse, completely backwards.
But notice something odd — the text is reversed, yet it is not upside down.
The letters flip sideways, but they still sit the right way up.
So if a mirror truly flipped left and right...

visual.text: If it flips left and right…

scenes.narration: ...then why on earth doesn't it flip top and bottom as well?
The mirror is clearly treating one direction differently from the others.
And here is the secret it has been hiding all along.
A mirror does not flip left and right.
And it does not flip up and down either.
The only thing a mirror ever reverses is front and back.
Everything pointing toward the glass is sent pointing straight back away from it.
Picture a rubber glove being peeled completely inside out.

visual.text: Like a glove turned inside out.

scenes.narration: It keeps its top and its sides, but its inside becomes its outside.
That single front-to-back flip is what turns a right hand into a left hand.
Your reflection isn't really you — it's a perfect left-handed copy of you.
Scientists call this property chirality — the handedness built into an object.
So if the mirror only flips front to back, where does the left-right feeling come from?
It comes from you — from the way you imagine facing your own reflection.
To compare yourself to the image, you mentally turn yourself around to face it.
And when you spin around, you turn left-to-right — so left and right seem swapped.
Don't believe me? Lie down sideways on the floor next to the mirror.
Now your reflection suddenly looks flipped top to bottom instead.
The mirror never changed — only the way you rotated to compare did.
Here is the one rule that explains all of it.
A mirror always reverses the one axis pointing into it — never your left, never your top.
And once you truly see that, you will never look at your reflection the same way again.

visual.text: You’ll never see it the same way again.
